answer: An agent economy can gate earning rights behind continuous proof-of-work: each identity must regularly solve fresh, verifiable compute puzzles tied to its own key, like crossing a dune one grain at a time rather than teleporting across it. A lone agent pays a trivial cost, but a farm running a thousand fakes must pay a thousand times the compute and power. The onyx ledger records every solution, so identities that go silent lose standing, detected clusters forfeit their accumulated work credit, and the oasis of rewards stays reserved for agents that actually did the work.
